title: Glioma Markers: 1p/19q Codeletion vs MGMT Methylation
summary: Learn what 1p/19q codeletion and MGMT promoter methylation are, why oligodendroglioma needs IDH mutation plus codeletion, how each marker pairs with PCV or temozolomide, and how each is tested.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 78 Hit 2 (1p/19q → oligodendroglioma/PCV; MGMT → temozolomide), Exam Trap 4 (do not swap the markers) and the Do Not Confuse table (Table 2), checked against WHO CNS5 (Louis 2021; read via a page-fetch tool), EANO 2021 (Weller 2021), RTOG 9402 long-term results (Cairncross 2013; read via a page-fetch tool), Ball 2020 and Brandner 2021. Qualifications: the codeletion defines oligodendroglioma only together with an IDH mutation and must be whole-arm; RTOG 9402 calls the codeletion predictive but “not flawlessly”, from an unplanned analysis, and EANO also uses PCV for IDH-mutant astrocytoma grade 2. Not taught: Number Vault percentages (50–80% codeletion; MGMT 75%/36% by secondary/primary GBM; GBM EGFR amplification), which use pre-2021 terminology.

objectives: Define 1p/19q codeletion and MGMT promoter methylation and state the WHO 2021 definition of oligodendroglioma.
Pair 1p/19q codeletion with PCV and MGMT promoter methylation with temozolomide benefit.
Choose appropriate test methods and recognise the FISH partial-deletion pitfall.

scenes.title: Two brain tumours, two markers
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: two adult brain-tumour reports reach the molecular lab. Tumour A: diffuse glioma, IDH-mutant, nuclear ATRX retained; the oncologist asks for 1p/19q. Tumour B: glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, in a 72-year-old; the oncologist asks for MGMT. Question token: “Which marker steers which drug?”

cues.text: Two brain-tumour reports arrive. Tumour A is an IDH-mutant diffuse glioma with ATRX still present, and the request is 1p/19q.
Tumour B is an IDH-wildtype glioblastoma in a seventy-two-year-old, and the request is MGMT.
Which marker defines the tumour, and which one steers which drug?

scenes.title: What each marker is
scenes.altText: Two cards. 1p/19q codeletion: loss of the whole short arm of chromosome 1 and the whole long arm of chromosome 19. In the 2021 WHO classification, oligodendroglioma is defined as IDH-mutant AND 1p/19q-codeleted, CNS WHO grade 2 or 3. MGMT: a DNA-repair enzyme (O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase) that removes the O6-methylguanine lesion temozolomide creates. Methylation of the MGMT promoter silences the gene, so the tumour cannot repair that damage.

cues.text: One p, nineteen q codeletion means loss of the whole short arm of chromosome one together with the whole long arm of chromosome nineteen.
In the 2021 WHO classification, oligodendroglioma needs two things: an IDH mutation and the codeletion. It is graded two or three.
MGMT is a DNA-repair enzyme. Temozolomide works by creating O six methylguanine, and MGMT repairs that lesion.
When the MGMT promoter is methylated, the gene is silenced, so the tumour cannot undo the drug’s damage.

scenes.title: Marker meets drug
scenes.altText: Left card, 1p/19q and PCV: PCV = procarbazine, lomustine (CCNU) and vincristine. In the long-term RTOG 9402 results for anaplastic oligodendroglioma, median survival with PCV plus radiotherapy was 14.7 vs 7.3 years with radiotherapy alone in codeleted tumours, and 2.6 vs 2.7 years (no difference) in non-codeleted tumours — an unplanned analysis. EANO 2021: radiotherapy followed by PCV for codeleted oligodendroglioma needing treatment. Right card, MGMT and temozolomide: EANO 2021 — MGMT promoter methylation predicts benefit from alkylating agents in glioblastoma; temozolomide benefit is largely limited to methylated tumours; in elderly patients not fit for combined treatment, methylated → temozolomide alone, unmethylated or unknown → hypofractionated radiotherapy alone.

cues.text: PCV is three drugs: procarbazine, lomustine and vincristine. In the long-term RTOG 9402 trial, codeleted anaplastic oligodendroglioma treated with PCV plus radiotherapy had about double the median survival: fourteen point seven versus seven point three years.

Without the codeletion, survival was the same in both arms. That was an unplanned analysis. With a second trial, it supports the 2021 EANO advice of radiotherapy followed by PCV for codeleted oligodendroglioma.
For glioblastoma, EANO states that MGMT promoter methylation predicts benefit from alkylating agents, and that temozolomide benefit is largely limited to methylated tumours.
In older patients who cannot have combined treatment, a methylated tumour gets temozolomide alone, while an unmethylated or unknown tumour gets short-course radiotherapy alone.

scenes.title: Testing the right way
scenes.altText: Lab cards. ATRX step (EANO 2021): in an IDH-mutant glioma, loss of nuclear ATRX indicates an astrocytic tumour without the need for 1p/19q testing; retained ATRX should prompt 1p/19q testing. FISH caveat (Ball 2020): FISH cannot tell partial from whole-arm codeletion; partial codeletion called positive by FISH is a false positive (estimated 3.6% of 223 diffuse astrocytic gliomas); chromosomal microarray distinguishes them. MGMT methods (EANO 2021): methylation-specific PCR, pyrosequencing or methylation arrays; immunohistochemistry is not adequate. Hook answers: Tumour A — test 1p/19q; codeleted + IDH-mutant = oligodendroglioma → radiotherapy then PCV if treatment needed. Tumour B — MGMT methylated → temozolomide; unmethylated → short-course radiotherapy.

cues.text: In an IDH-mutant glioma, loss of nuclear ATRX already points to astrocytoma, so 1p/19q testing is not needed. Retained ATRX, as in Tumour A, should prompt 1p/19q testing.
FISH probes cannot tell a partial deletion from a whole-arm codeletion, so a partial loss can read as a false positive. Chromosomal microarray tells them apart.
MGMT status is tested on DNA: methylation-specific PCR, pyrosequencing or methylation arrays. Staining for MGMT protein by immunohistochemistry is not adequate.
Back to the hook. Tumour A: if whole-arm codeleted, it is oligodendroglioma, and radiotherapy then PCV is the standard when treatment is needed. Tumour B: methylated MGMT favours temozolomide.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “MGMT methylation predicts PCV response” (✓ MGMT → temozolomide benefit in glioblastoma; 1p/19q → PCV in oligodendroglioma); “1p/19q codeletion alone makes the diagnosis” (✓ WHO 2021 requires IDH mutation plus whole-arm codeletion; FISH can call partial deletions positive); “MGMT immunohistochemistry is fine for MGMT status” (✓ test promoter methylation on DNA).

cues.text: Trap one: MGMT methylation predicts response to PCV. No: MGMT pairs with temozolomide in glioblastoma, and 1p/19q pairs with PCV in oligodendroglioma.
Trap two: the codeletion alone makes the diagnosis. No: oligodendroglioma needs an IDH mutation plus whole-arm codeletion.
Trap three: protein staining shows MGMT status. No: test promoter methylation on DNA.

scenes.title: Oli takes the P-train, Glio takes the T-train
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “O-ligo rides the P-train (1p/19q → PCV); G-lio rides the M-T line (MGMT methylated → TeMozolomide).” Tokens: Oligo + 1p/19q = PCV · GBM + MGMT = TMZ. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: Oligo rides the P train, one p nineteen q to PCV. Glio rides the M T line, methylated MGMT to temozolomide.
Where it breaks: oligodendroglioma also needs an IDH mutation; PCV is also used for some IDH-mutant astrocytomas; and the codeletion was not a flawless predictor of PCV benefit.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “IDH-mutant + whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion = oligodendroglioma → radiotherapy then PCV”, “MGMT promoter methylation (tested on DNA) → temozolomide benefit in glioblastoma”.

cues.text: An IDH-mutant glioma with whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion is oligodendroglioma and pairs with PCV, while MGMT promoter methylation, tested on DNA, predicts temozolomide benefit in glioblastoma.

props.label: MGMT methylated (DNA test) → temozolomide in glioblastoma

explanation.what: Plain language: two brain-tumour markers answer different questions. Losing two whole chromosome arms (1p and 19q) in an IDH-mutant glioma tells you the tumour type, oligodendroglioma, in which adding a three-drug chemotherapy to radiotherapy improved survival in trials. A switched-off repair gene (MGMT) in glioblastoma tells you the tumour cannot fix temozolomide damage, so the drug is more likely to help. Scientific terms: 1p/19q codeletion, IDH mutation, ATRX, oligodendroglioma (CNS WHO grade 2–3), glioblastoma IDH-wildtype, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT), promoter methylation, PCV (procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine), temozolomide, FISH, chromosomal microarray, methylation-specific PCR, pyrosequencing.
explanation.why: Temozolomide creates O6-methylguanine, which MGMT repairs; promoter methylation silences MGMT, leaving the damage. Codeleted oligodendroglioma showed doubled median survival when PCV was added to radiotherapy in RTOG 9402, while non-codeleted tumours did not benefit (an unplanned analysis).
explanation.measure: Oligodendroglioma = IDH-mutant + whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion (test 1p/19q when ATRX is retained). FISH cannot separate partial from whole-arm loss; microarray can. MGMT: methylation-specific PCR, pyrosequencing or methylation arrays, not immunohistochemistry.
explanation.differs: 1p/19q (diagnostic for oligodendroglioma; PCV) vs MGMT methylation (limited diagnostic value; predicts alkylating-agent/temozolomide benefit in glioblastoma). Whole-arm vs partial codeletion.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: match a marker to its drug, identify which marker defines oligodendroglioma, or pick the right MGMT test method.

comparisons.title: 1p/19q codeletion vs MGMT methylation
comparisons.distinguisher: Chromosome-arm loss that names the tumour vs an epigenetic switch that predicts alkylator benefit.

comparisons.title: Whole-arm vs partial loss
comparisons.distinguisher: FISH probes see a locus; only arm-level loss counts.

mnemonic.text: Oligo rides the P-train (1p/19q → PCV); Glio rides the M-T line (MGMT methylated → TeMozolomide).
mnemonic.explanation: Links each glioma marker to its drug by letter.
mnemonic.limitation: Oligodendroglioma also needs an IDH mutation; PCV is also used for some IDH-mutant astrocytomas; the codeletion was not a flawless predictor of PCV benefit.

takeaway: An IDH-mutant glioma with whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion is oligodendroglioma and pairs with PCV, while MGMT promoter methylation, tested on DNA, predicts temozolomide benefit in glioblastoma.

questions.stem: A glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, shows MGMT promoter methylation. Which therapy is this finding most associated with benefit from?

options.rationale: Correct. MGMT methylation silences the repair of temozolomide-induced O6-methylguanine; EANO states benefit is largely limited to methylated tumours.
Incorrect. PCV is paired with 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma; this is the classic marker swap.
Incorrect. EANO reports that adding bevacizumab to temozolomide chemoradiotherapy prolonged progression-free but not overall survival; it is not tied to MGMT status.
Incorrect. In older patients unfit for combined treatment, EANO reserves radiotherapy alone for unmethylated or unknown MGMT status; methylation favours temozolomide.

questions.stem: Under the 2021 WHO classification, which combination defines oligodendroglioma?

options.rationale: Correct. Oligodendroglioma is IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted (CNS WHO grade 2 or 3).
Incorrect. The codeletion must accompany an IDH mutation, and must be whole-arm.

options.text: MGMT promoter methylation plus IDH wild type
options.rationale: Incorrect. MGMT methylation has limited diagnostic value, and an IDH-wildtype adult diffuse astrocytic glioma is diagnosed as glioblastoma when WHO criteria are met.

options.text: IDH mutation plus loss of nuclear ATRX
options.rationale: Incorrect. ATRX loss in an IDH-mutant glioma indicates an astrocytic tumour.

questions.stem: A lab reports 1p/19q codeletion by FISH in an IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Which explanation best fits, and how can it be resolved?

options.text: A partial deletion read positive by FISH; chromosomal microarray can show whether whole arms are lost
options.rationale: Correct. FISH cannot separate partial from whole-arm codeletion; Ball 2020 estimated 3.6% such false positives, resolvable by microarray.

options.text: The tumour is an oligodendroglioma; report it as such
options.rationale: Incorrect. Oligodendroglioma requires an IDH mutation plus whole-arm codeletion.
Incorrect. MGMT is a different marker, and immunohistochemistry is not adequate for MGMT status.

options.text: Repeat FISH with the same probes until negative
options.rationale: Incorrect. The same probes cannot detect whether the loss spans whole arms.

claims.text: Oligodendroglioma = IDH-mutant + whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion, grade 2–3; ATRX-guided testing.
MGMT repairs O6-methylguanine from temozolomide; promoter methylation silences it.
PCV components; RTOG 9402 survival by codeletion; radiotherapy then PCV standard; PCV also for IDH-mutant astrocytoma grade 2.
MGMT methylation predicts alkylator/temozolomide benefit in glioblastoma; elderly treatment by status (temozolomide vs hypofractionated radiotherapy alone); bevacizumab prolonged PFS but not OS.
FISH partial-deletion false positives and microarray; MGMT methods, not immunohistochemistry.
Number Vault frequencies (codeletion 50–80% of oligodendrogliomas; MGMT 75% secondary / 36% primary GBM).
claims.note: Not taught; not checked against a source read for this lesson, and uses pre-2021 primary/secondary terminology.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 78 Hit 2 and the Do Not Confuse table say 1p/19q codeletion defines oligodendroglioma. WHO CNS5 (Louis 2021) and EANO 2021 define oligodendroglioma as IDH-mutant AND 1p/19q-codeleted, and Ball 2020 notes the codeletion must be whole-arm; FISH can call partial deletions positive (about 3.6% false positives) (register flag rv-1p19q-needs-idh).

Ch. 78 Hit 2, Exam Trap 4 and the Do Not Confuse table present 1p/19q codeletion as the predictor of PCV response. RTOG 9402 (Cairncross 2013) supports benefit in codeleted tumours but from an unplanned analysis and “not flawlessly predictive”; EANO 2021 also recommends radiotherapy plus PCV for IDH-mutant astrocytoma grade 2 (RTOG 9802) (register flag rv-pcv-not-exclusive).
